title: Halving as Undoing Doubling
objective: Halving an even number is the inverse of doubling — if double 6 is 12, then half of 12 is 6.
studentQuestion: If doubling 6 gives 12, what should half of 12 give back?
newIdea: Halving explicitly framed as doubling's inverse operation, not a new, unrelated skill.

teaching.setup: The known fact 6 + 6 = 12, already on display.
teaching.see: If 6 and 6 make 12, what is half of 12?
teaching.break: Read the bond backward: 12 splits into two equal parts.
teaching.build: State half of 12 is 6, using the already-known double.
teaching.transform: 6 + 6 = 12 and half of 12 = 6 — the same relationship, read in opposite directions.

check.prompt: Double the answer (6) back to confirm it returns 12.

examples.transfer: Half of 20, using the known double-10 fact.

mastery.evidence: Correctly states half of 3 even numbers using their known doubles facts, and explains the inverse relationship.
